title.value: Robustness and sample complexity of model-based MARL for general-sum Markov games

extractions.description: A theoretical paper studying the robustness of Markov perfect equilibria to model approximation in general-sum Markov games, and deriving Hoeffding- and Bernstein-type sample complexity bounds for model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning with a generative model. A small numerical example (3-state, 2-player game) with 1,000 simulated experiments illustrates the bounds.

type.quote:
In this paper, we investigate the fundamental question of sample complexity for model-based MARL algorithms in general-sum Markov games. We
show two results.
type.justification: The paper proves theorems and corollaries about approximation and sample complexity; numerical examples only illustrate the theory.
